sectional-builder-45-handoff.objective: Make the Sectional Builder left and right 45-degree previews read as one physically connected sofa. Both views must show the same assembly from opposite front corners without inside-out arms, detached return modules, cushions showing through structural backs, or ottomans acquiring backs.

working.item: Straight 3-seat and 2-seat presets are visually coherent in both views.
Straight sofa plus chaise is mostly coherent in both views.
Sofa plus ottoman is mostly coherent and the ottoman remains backless.
Arms, seat cushions, structural backs, and loose back cushions are separate semantic surfaces.
Every surface has data-sb-review-part metadata for targeted visual review.

broken.item: L-shape and L-shape-plus-chaise return rows appear exploded or disconnected, especially in Right 45.
Rotated return backs can look like oversized freestanding panels.
Changing painter order changes which artifact is visible but does not make the return physically coherent.
Some arm faces still read inside-out from the opposite camera angle.
Flat SVG polygon painter ordering is being asked to resolve intersecting module geometry without a reliable physical layout.

root-cause-analysis.cause: The editable plan uses a forgiving fixed grid where CELL is 132 pixels. The 45-degree renderer also used this grid as product-space geometry. Consequently 90 cm, 100 cm, and 105 cm modules all commonly become one 132-pixel tile, while a 160 cm chaise becomes two tiles. This means dimensions, rotations, and connector positions are not represented by one consistent physical coordinate system.

A previous test required left and right views to use the identical module paint sequence because screen x is mirrored. That assumption is false. Screen projection may mirror, but camera depth changes between opposite front corners. Asymmetric assemblies require camera-specific paint order.

Whole-module sorting keeps each module anatomically coherent but cannot resolve a true L intersection where one edge of a return is behind the corner and another is in front. Global surface sorting can represent that intersection, but only if every surface has correct world coordinates and depth. Layer-rank-first global sorting previously split modules badly.

work-completed-this-pass.item: Replaced the invalid same-paint-sequence unit test with a camera-specific depth expectation. Before the interrupted refactor, 60/60 unit tests passed.
Changed the renderer from whole-module painter ordering to global surface-depth ordering with semantic layer, piece, and source-order tie-breaks.
Ran the 12-case visual matrix. Surface sorting alone did not repair the L-shape geometry, proving that ordering is not the sole defect.

important-partial-change.warning: A centimetre-derived ProductLayout refactor has been partially applied to src/modules/ui/sectional-builder.ts and may not currently type-check. Do not assume the branch is green.

added.item: createProductLayout(pieces), using exact module dimensions for column and row offsets.
productProjection now accepts ProductLayout and derives bounds from physical placements.

still-required.item: Create the layout in sectionalProductMarkup before productProjection.
Pass layout into every sectionalProductPieceLayers call.
Run npx tsc --noEmit immediately and fix all signature errors.

recommended-implementation.step: Finish the ProductLayout wiring and restore a clean type-check. Do not change the editable plan grid or saved project format.
Define product-space placement from explicit connector alignment rather than merely summing row and column maxima. A rotated return must attach its local connector to the corner connector exactly.
Give each rendered surface a stable depth interval, not only a center depth point. Use far-to-near surface ordering and split a polygon only if two connected surfaces genuinely cross in projection.

Keep capability rules explicit by PieceKind. Ottoman has no back frame or back cushion. Corner has two structural back planes. Perpendicular return upholstery must obey camera visibility rather than a blanket hide rule.

Render arm outer panel, inner panel, front end, rear end, and top cap as separate surfaces. Cull faces by transformed normal for each camera. Do not infer the visible arm face from left/right screen position.
Compare all six presets in both views after every geometry change. Do not update the screenshot baseline until all twelve cells are coherent.

assertions.item: No ottoman back-frame or back-cushion surface.
No connected module gap larger than the outline width.
No loose back cushion visible through a camera-facing structural back.
No contradictory inner and outer arm panels visible simultaneously.
Both views contain the same modules but may use different paint sequences.
Every module surface retains semantic data-sb-review-part metadata.

do-not-repeat.item: Do not force identical paint order for Left 45 and Right 45.
Do not update the visual snapshot merely because the diff is stable.
Do not fix only the currently selected preset; use the full 12-view sheet.
Do not modify the plan-grid persistence format to solve a product-view-only issue.
Do not use broad per-camera hacks that hide an entire semantic category.
